solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild diatribe interrupting female in charge

indicators.note: a diatribe that interrupts something breaks into it, so it sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a diatribe is a rant

explanation.surface: An angry outburst cuts across the woman who is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wild with worry or rage is beside themselves, which is a synonym sense of the answer.

clue.text: Bill of fare excludes escargots for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so here the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu that leaves out snails among its first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill of fare' looks like the definition (a menu), but only 'Bill' defines; 'of' is a link and the starters come from fare, excludes, escargots.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill for a service is a charge, and a charge levied for a service is a synonym.

clue.text: Fundamentally, the answer lies in technique

indicators.note: one thing lying in another is placed inside it, so the first pieces go into the word for technique

parts.note: art can mean skill or technique, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A teacher's remark that the key to a problem is really a matter of method.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so deep down, in its essential nature, is an idiom meaning basically.

clue.text: Set fire to rubbish piled up next to church

indicators.note: in a down clue, something piled up is built upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone burns a heap of junk stacked beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'piled up' means read upwards; 'next to' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a building to the flame deliberately is to torch it, a verb synonym for arson.

clue.text: Meal provider — someone tending to consume a lot of tea

indicators.note: something that consumes another takes it inside, so the carer's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a carer is someone who tends to the sick or elderly

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, here with its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A cook who is also a nurse drinks a great deal of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'someone tending to' looks like 'inclined to', but the 'to' belongs with 'consume', the containment signal; 'a lot of' drops the drink's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for functions, so a provider of meals is a direct description.

clue.text: Insincere talk about a collection of books

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Hollow chatter on the subject of a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, pious-sounding talk, the sense of empty moral speech.

clue.text: Fold the first pieces of crêpe paper around the edge

indicators.note: the first two letters go around the word for edge, enclosing it
the first pieces of words are their opening letters

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Instructions for folding crêpe paper over at its border.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press into small folds or ridges, as with a pie crust or hair.

clue.text: Thing amazingly preceding Californian autumn sunset

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a startling way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, and California is in the US

explanation.surface: Something remarkable comes before a sunset in a Californian autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preceding' only sets the order, already that of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the coming of darkness at the end of the day, the time of the sun going down.

clue.text: Separate the ropes, partly for fastening

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to untangle the ropes, partly to tie something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain for tying an animal, so it serves as a fastening.

clue.text: After match, get endless sharp pain

parts.note: a twin is a match, something exactly alike

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A player picks up a sudden stab of pain after the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sporting fixture, but it means a counterpart or double; 'endless' cuts the final letter of 'get'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a brief, sudden stab of pain, such as one felt in a joint.

clue.text: A mix of hate and respect for favoured pupil

indicators.note: a mix blends things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Classmates' mixed feelings, loathing and admiration, towards the class favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the student a teacher visibly prefers over the rest.

clue.text: Utensils made using soapstone, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cutlery that may have been carved out of a soft stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made using' only links; soapstone is a soft carvable mineral, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaspoons are small spoons, examples of the kitchen and table implements called utensils.

clue.text: Friend returning item of clothing and computer

indicators.note: returning means the word for friend comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a top is a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: A friend gives back a shirt along with a computer that was borrowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer small enough to rest on the knees.

clue.text: Specialist trial demo

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is a specialist
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An expert's tryout of a demonstration version of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demo' looks like a demonstration of a product; here it is a political demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Demo is short for demonstration, a public march or rally voicing objection.

clue.text: Disreputable person is great socially, from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A rogue who is good company in a social setting, at least occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and sixth letters onwards of 'great socially'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest rogue, someone without a good reputation.

clue.text: I told you, her toe's broken!

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone smugly points out that a woman's toe is indeed fractured.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said in triumph after being proved right, just as one says I told you.

clue.text: A pretty cold, agitated old reptile

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone quite chilly and anxious, described like a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty cold' reads as 'fairly chilly' but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pterodactyl was a prehistoric flying reptile, so it is a long-extinct, ancient one.

clue.text: Come in the main front gate, or always at the back

indicators.note: always at the back means every word supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Directions to a visitor about which gate to use at a large house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' and 'back' look like a choice of entrances, but every word gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place, the same meaning as being invited to step inside.

clue.text: A party with sailors below deck

parts.note: a do is a party
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A party held by sailors in the lower part of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below deck' looks like a ship phrase, but 'deck' is the verb meaning decorate; 'below' just places RN under DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something, as in deck the halls, is to decorate or adorn it.

clue.text: Arrange one European trip

parts.note: to sort is to arrange
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Planning a journey for a single person across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a short outing or excursion, originally a military sally.

clue.text: Nervous individual departs, say, after returning

parts.note: one means a single individual
D is the abbreviation for departs, as on a timetable

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for say is turned back to front

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An anxious person leaves after coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies only to the abbreviation for 'say'; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being tense, jumpy and anxious.

clue.text: Sentimental stuff is fine, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, its last letter lost

parts.note: good means fine

explanation.surface: A shrug that soppy material is largely all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is informal for mawkish sentiment, cloying stuff like a sticky substance.

clue.text: One employing some house rules

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An employer setting a few rules for the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who makes use of something, one who uses or employs it.

clue.text: Fruit gelato served up without nuts on top

indicators.note: food served up is dished out in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
on top points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ice cream dish brought out without its topping of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like an instruction to remove the nuts, but it reads as 'with', so N joins GELATO before 'served up' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.
